topStories.headline: Three Days to Go: District 10's Supervisor Race Comes Down to Data Centers, Surveillance, and Who Pays the Price
topStories.dek: With Election Day on November 3, the contest to replace termed-out Supervisor Shamann Walton has crystallized around what Bayview-Hunters Point owes San Francisco's AI economy.
topStories.body:
Voters in District 10 — which covers Bayview-Hunters Point, Visitacion Valley, Dogpatch, and Potrero Hill — head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 to choose a new supervisor for the first time since Shamann Walton won the seat in 2018. Walton terms out in January. Mission Local's ongoing Meet the Candidates series, updated this week, has focused the contest on three frontrunners: Theo Ellington, Dion-Jay "DJ" Brookter, and J.R. Eppler.

The race has turned substantially on the question of AI data centers. On October 6, the full Board of Supervisors passed Walton's 45-day moratorium on new data center construction, freezing a planned expansion of the NOVVA facility at 400 Paul Avenue in south-central Bayview. Five large data center campuses already operate on or near Paul Avenue, directly across from residential blocks. The San Francisco Planning Commission now has 45 days to assess whether those facilities pose an environmental threat to nearby residents.

All three leading candidates have backed the moratorium, but they differ on how far to go. Brookter, endorsed by Walton, has called for a permanent ban. Ellington told Mission Local this month that he now supports an all-out ban on new data centers — a harder line than his earlier moratorium-with-conditions position — and said he would not renew SFPD's contract with Flock Safety, the company whose AI-enhanced license-plate cameras blanket Hunters Point. Eppler has also backed the moratorium.

Ellington received a $500,000 contribution in September from Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen, reported to be the largest outside donation in a San Francisco supervisor's race in recent memory. Ellington has said the donor does not speak for his campaign. By Ethics Commission figures, Ellington's own fundraising stands at roughly $488,000; Eppler raised about $182,000; and Brookter about $179,000.

For Bayview residents, the issues are immediate. Hunters Point Community Biomonitoring published a pilot proposal in October calling for a one-year program to track residents' bodily exposure to pollution, noise, and heat from the Paul Avenue campus — arguing that no comprehensive monitoring system currently exists even as the first phase of NOVVA's planned 36-megawatt complex has been operating since this summer.

topStories.headline: SFPD Closes Two Separate Bayview Homicide Cases With Arrests on the Same Morning
topStories.dek: On October 20, police announced homicide arrests in two unrelated cases — one involving a 44-year-old San Francisco man, the other a juvenile — both tied to shootings in Bayview earlier this month.
topStories.body:
San Francisco police announced on the morning of October 20 that investigators had made arrests in two separate Bayview homicide cases, posting the news to the SFPD Bayview Station page within 30 minutes of each other.

In the first case (SFPD Case #260-577-378), officers arrested Jorge Alberto Mendoza-Hernandez, 44, of San Francisco, on suspicion of killing a man near the 1100 block of Thomas Avenue on October 1 — a largely industrial street bordering the Yosemite Slough waterfront in Hunters Point. The victim was transported to Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, where he died from his injuries. Detectives obtained a Ramey warrant and arrested Mendoza-Hernandez on the 600 block of Gilman Avenue in Bayview on October 16. He was booked on a homicide charge.

In the second case (SFPD Case #260-611-578), police arrested a juvenile male in connection with the fatal shooting of a man on the 1100 block of Wisconsin Street on October 16 at approximately 8:38 p.m. Officers found the victim suffering from multiple gunshot wounds; he died at the scene despite paramedics' efforts. Investigators served a search warrant on the 1800 block of 25th Street on October 17, where they arrested the suspect and seized evidence. Because the suspect is a minor, SFPD did not release his name or age. He was transported to the Juvenile Justice Center and booked for homicide under California Penal Code 187(a).

Both investigations remain open and active. Anyone with information is asked to contact SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411, beginning the message with SFPD.

moreNews.headline: Biomonitoring Group Calls for Health Tracking Study at Bayview's Paul Avenue Data Center Campus
moreNews.body: Hunters Point Community Biomonitoring published a pilot proposal on October 12 calling for a one-year program to measure residents' exposure to pollution, noise, dirty air, and heat generated by the AI data center campus on Paul Avenue in south-central Bayview. The group argues that no comprehensive monitoring system currently exists, even as the NOVVA facility — part of a planned 36-megawatt build-out — brought its initial 9-megawatt phase online this summer. The San Francisco Bay View reported that the proposal aims to document a health baseline for residents before the costs of the city's AI expansion become irreversible.

moreNews.headline: Crocker Amazon Ballfield Overhaul Still Awaiting Board of Supervisors Vote
moreNews.body: As of Mission Local's September 25 report, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors had not yet scheduled a vote on the proposed $28 million grant from the San Francisco Giants Community Fund to rebuild the ballfields at Crocker Amazon Park. The Recreation and Park Commission voted unanimously in April 2026 to recommend the board accept the grant, which would fund synthetic turf on five of six renovated fields and require removing about 128 mature trees. Opponents organized as Keep Crocker Real have continued pressing the mayor and supervisors to revise the design. Rec & Park has said a further round of community review must be completed before any final approval, with groundbreaking not expected before 2027 or 2028 at the earliest.
